newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, June 6 - CPO production in May turned out to be somewhat better than earlier expectations. Partial data available indicate production rose an estimated 7 percent or around 50,000 tonnes to 784,000 tonnes. This is nearly 4 percent higher than our previous estimate. The better performance reflected mainly improved oil extraction rate (OER), especially in Peninsular Malaysia. Compared to May last year production registered a growth of an estimated 8.6 percent, down slightly from the 10.9 percent growth recorded in January-April.
CPO offtake, in contrast, declined marginally.

Sales of CPO in May also fell around 30 percent when compared to April. This reflected a slowdown in new export sales of products for shipments from June onwards. Exports of palm oil in May meanwhile are estimated to have risen to 635,000 tonnes from 570,000 reported by PORLA and our estimate of 610,000 for April. Stocks of palm oil are estimated to have risen to 745,000 tonnes from around 698,000 tonnes in April and 715,200 tonnes in May last year. Virtually all the increase in stocks was in the form of CPO which rose to an estimated 395,000 tonnes from around 350,000 tonnes a month earlier. Also the bulk of the rise in CPO stocks occured in Peninsular Malaysia.

Despite a surge in palm oil exports in the last 10 days of May which ensured an overall increase in offtake for the whole month, prices took a downturn right from the start of this month due to players focussing more on the slow pace in new export sales and prospects for a contraction in June shipments. Sentiments were further undermined by weakness in CBOT soy complex as well as concern over increased competition from Indonesian palm oil exporters. Yesterday, CPO futures opened 12 ringgit lower, bringing the cumulative losses since Monday to some 50 ringgit.
Yesterday, the August contract settled at 1,198 ringgit, down from 1,219 ringgit on Monday, June 2. August/September RBD olein was quoted at $552.50, down from $565 on Monday.

Thereafter the market staged a rebound to close near the high and 3-6 ringgit higher than the preceding day. The drop in price generated moderate new exports sales to Egypt and China in the last two days. The rebound is however likely to falter unless there is follow through buying in the export market in the coming weeks. In the absence of a weather market developing in any major producing-importing/exporting country in the next several weeks, we see difficulty in CPO futures retracing to the 1,220 ringgit level, basis the active third month contract.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters)
